run.goal: Fix one demonstrated control UI defect from current GitHub main (258318458f42406dc5a519dd72563e1548fc4c48 or its newer descendant). Use normal repository synchronization, not an explicit older run snapshot. In browser/control.ts, refresh only calls show(state) when protectedErrorVersion !== viewVersion. After a failed start/cancel/resume action this condition stays false until another action, freezing status, CAPTCHA affordances, counts and Annonces even while /api/status succeeds. Preserve a useful readable action error without suppressing fresh collection state and retained announcements indefinitely. Keep stale-response protection, no overlapping resume, current retained-card behavior and safe text/link rendering. Make the smallest coherent TypeScript source change and update its generated deliverable using the existing build path. Add and execute one focused offline UI regression demonstrating a failed action followed by changed successful status/rows updating without another action or page reload, while the error remains readable and an older response cannot overwrite newer action state. Reuse saved delivery evidence from 84ae80d1 and current main for already established behavior; do not rerun old CAPTCHA/Annonces suites, npm ci/check or a general audit just for badges. Use targeted test, type/lint checks and necessary build only. Do not change CAPTCHA classification, collector behavior, historical data/evidence or test discovery exclusions. Synthetic offline fixtures only; no live xe.gr/Spitogatos, personal browser profiles, real cookies, hosting, client acceptance or publication.

runAssessment.summary: The run was cancelled by an external shutdown after 426 seconds and $0.208, rather than failing. Before cancellation it implemented and built the focused UI change, passed the focused browser regression, typecheck, and lint, and responded to a root rejection by strengthening stale-response ordering evidence. The final validation/recovery cycle had only just opened, so no delivery was claimed. The spend reflects three materially different execution attempts and progressively stronger evidence rather than an identical-call loop.

findings.title: Cancellation interrupted a promising second acceptance cycle
findings.detail: The first root pass correctly rejected final-state-only evidence as unable to distinguish a transient stale overwrite. The subsequent execution added ordering assertions and passed a focused regression, but cancellation occurred as another coached planning turn opened, before a new acceptance verdict. This is a policy interruption, not evidence that the implementation was defective.
